from manim import *
import random

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Objective: Shrinking the Search Space"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Wordle is about narrowing down 2,315 secret words.',
            'Your first guess should eliminate the most candidates.',
            'High-frequency letters shrink the search space faster.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color change only for active line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # A dense cloud of 2,315 small white (#FFFFFF) dots fills the screen to represent the word pool.
        # We constrain the cloud to the grid area on the right side.
        num_dots = 2315
        dots = VGroup()
        random.seed(42) # Consistent random distribution
        
        # Grid boundaries: x [0.0, 6.0], y [-3.3, 2.7]
        for _ in range(num_dots):
            pos_x = random.uniform(0.1, 5.9)
            pos_y = random.uniform(-3.2, 2.6)
            dot = Dot(point=[pos_x, pos_y, 0], radius=0.015, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.7)
            dots.add(dot)
        
        # Show the cloud population
        self.play(FadeIn(dots, lag_ratio=0.0001), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The word 'FUZZY' appears in grey (#787C7E) boxes
        fuzzy_word = self.create_wordle_word("FUZZY", "#787C7E")
        self.place_in_area(fuzzy_word, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(fuzzy_word, shift=UP*0.2))
        
        # "only a tiny fraction of dots vanish"
        # Since FUZZY is an inefficient guess, we eliminate very few dots.
        num_fuzzy_removed = 75 
        all_indices = list(range(num_dots))
        random.shuffle(all_indices)
        fuzzy_indices = all_indices[:num_fuzzy_removed]
        remaining_indices = all_indices[num_fuzzy_removed:]
        
        dots_to_remove_fuzzy = VGroup(*[dots[i] for i in fuzzy_indices])
        self.play(FadeOut(dots_to_remove_fuzzy), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The word 'TRACE' appears in grey (#787C7E) boxes
        trace_word = self.create_wordle_word("TRACE", "#787C7E")
        self.place_in_area(trace_word, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Contrast with previous guess
        self.play(FadeOut(fuzzy_word), FadeIn(trace_word))
        
        # "a massive portion of dots vanish instantly"
        # TRACE is highly efficient, eliminating ~90% of the pool.
        num_remaining = len(remaining_indices)
        num_trace_removed = int(num_remaining * 0.93)
        trace_indices = remaining_indices[:num_trace_removed]
        
        dots_to_remove_trace = VGroup(*[dots[i] for i in trace_indices])
        self.play(FadeOut(dots_to_remove_trace), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(3)

    def create_wordle_word(self, word, box_color):
        """Helper to create a row of Wordle-style boxes with letters."""
        word_group = VGroup()
        for letter in word:
            square = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_color=box_color, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2, stroke_color=WHITE)
            char = Text(letter, font_size=28, color=WHITE, weight=BOLD)
            word_group.add(VGroup(square, char))
        word_group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        return word_group

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'Entropy measures the reduction of uncertainty in bits.',
            'Each bit of information cuts possibilities in half.',
            'We seek guesses that maximize this information gain.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Understanding Entropy and Information Theory", lecture_lines)
        
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#5865F2" # Blue
        NODE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Root node
        root_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        root_label = Text("Total Words", font_size=16, color=NODE_COLOR)
        root_node = VGroup(root_circle, root_label)
        self.place_in_area(root_node, "A3", "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(root_circle), Write(root_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Level 1 Nodes
        node_l1_1 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        node_l1_2 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(node_l1_1, "C1", "C2")
        self.place_in_area(node_l1_2, "C5", "C6")
        
        # Level 2 Nodes
        node_l2_1 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        node_l2_2 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        node_l2_3 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        node_l2_4 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(node_l2_1, "E1", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(node_l2_2, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(node_l2_3, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(node_l2_4, "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Edges
        edge1 = Line(root_circle.get_bottom(), node_l1_1.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        edge2 = Line(root_circle.get_bottom(), node_l1_2.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        
        edge_l2_1 = Line(node_l1_1.get_bottom(), node_l2_1.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        edge_l2_2 = Line(node_l1_1.get_bottom(), node_l2_2.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        edge_l2_3 = Line(node_l1_2.get_bottom(), node_l2_3.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        edge_l2_4 = Line(node_l1_2.get_bottom(), node_l2_4.get_top(), color=NODE_COLOR)
        
        tree_edges = VGroup(edge1, edge2, edge_l2_1, edge_l2_2, edge_l2_3, edge_l2_4)
        tree_nodes = VGroup(node_l1_1, node_l1_2, node_l2_1, node_l2_2, node_l2_3, node_l2_4)
        
        # Labels for halves
        half_label_1 = Text("50%", font_size=14, color=GRAY).next_to(edge1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        half_label_2 = Text("50%", font_size=14, color=GRAY).next_to(edge2, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(tree_edges),
            Create(tree_nodes),
            Write(half_label_1),
            Write(half_label_2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Highlight path
        path_highlight = VGroup(edge1, node_l1_1, edge_l2_2, node_l2_2)
        bit_label = Text("1 Bit Reduction", font_size=18, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(bit_label, "F1", "F3")
        
        self.play(
            path_highlight.animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).set_stroke(width=6),
            Write(bit_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines and Title
        title_str = "The Math: The 243 Possible Feedback Patterns"
        lines_str = [
            'Five positions with three colors yield 243 feedback patterns.',
            'Every guess maps the word list into these patterns.',
            'Optimal words distribute answers evenly across all buckets.',
            'Dense buckets leave too much uncertainty for the solver.',
            'Sparse distributions provide the most information on average.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_GREY = "#787C7E"
        COLOR_YELLOW = "#C9B458"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#6AAA64"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Blank Wordle Row
        wordle_row = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, stroke_color=COLOR_WHITE) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(wordle_row, "B1", "B6")
        
        # 3 Color Squares
        color_squares = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=COLOR_GREY, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0),
            Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=COLOR_YELLOW, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0),
            Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=COLOR_GREEN, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(color_squares, "A2", "A5")
        
        # Equation
        equation = Text("3^5 = 243", color=COLOR_WHITE, font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(equation, "C1", "C6")
        
        self.play(Create(wordle_row), FadeIn(color_squares), Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Histogram with 243 thin white bars
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.1, stroke_width=1.5, color=COLOR_WHITE) 
            for _ in range(243)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.01)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "F1", "F6")
        
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # SALET appears
        word_salet = Text("SALET", font_size=36, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(word_salet, "D2", "D5")
        
        # Dots distribute
        dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(radius=0.03, color=COLOR_WHITE).move_to(word_salet.get_center()) 
            for _ in range(50)
        ])
        
        # Distribution animation: bars grow evenly
        def grow_bars_even(mobjects):
            for i, bar in enumerate(mobjects):
                target_height = 0.4 + np.random.uniform(-0.1, 0.1)
                bar.scale(target_height / bar.get_height())
                bar.move_to(self.grid["F1"] + RIGHT * (i * 0.02) + UP * (bar.get_height()/2), coor_mask=np.array([1,1,0]))

        self.play(FadeIn(word_salet))
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[dot.animate.move_to(bars[np.random.randint(0, 243)].get_top()) for dot in dots], lag_ratio=0.05),
            *[bar.animate.scale(4) for bar in bars],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.remove(dots)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Dense buckets: few very tall bars, many zeros
        dense_animations = []
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            if i % 60 == 0: # 4 peaks
                dense_animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(1.5).set_color(COLOR_YELLOW))
            else:
                dense_animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.05).set_opacity(0.3))
        
        self.play(*dense_animations, run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Transition lecture highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Sparse distributions: back to even
        sparse_animations = []
        for bar in bars:
            sparse_animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.5).set_color(COLOR_WHITE).set_opacity(1.0))
            
        self.play(*sparse_animations, run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Section 4: Algorithmic Deep Dive",
            [
                "- Information Theory Basics",
                "- Calculating Expected Entropy",
                "- The Power of 'CRANE' and 'SALET'",
                "- Pruning the Search Space"
            ]
        )

        # 2. Visualizing Wordle Blocks in the grid
        wordle_squares = VGroup()
        letters = ["C", "R", "A", "N", "E"]
        colors = [GRAY, GRAY, YELLOW, GRAY, GREEN]

        for i, (char, col) in enumerate(zip(letters, colors)):
            # Create a box
            box = Square(side_length=0.7, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            box.set_fill(col, opacity=0.5)
            
            # Create letter
            char_mob = Text(char, font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            
            # Place in grid (Row A, Cols 1-5)
            grid_id = f"A{i+1}"
            self.place_at_grid(box, grid_id)
            char_mob.move_to(box.get_center())
            
            wordle_squares.add(VGroup(box, char_mob))

        # 3. Animate the word entry
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[FadeIn(sq, shift=DOWN) for sq in wordle_squares],
                lag_ratio=0.2
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Highlight Entropy Calculation (Conceptual)
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        entropy_math = Text(
            "E[I] = Σ p_i log2( 1 / p_i )",
            font_size=24,
            color=BLUE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(entropy_math, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        entropy_math.shift(RIGHT * 0.5) # Slight manual adjustment for visibility
        
        self.play(Write(entropy_math))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Connect concepts
        arrow = Arrow(
            wordle_squares[2].get_bottom(),
            entropy_math.get_top(),
            buff=0.2,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        
        analysis_text = Text("High Entropy Split", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        analysis_text.next_to(arrow, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(analysis_text))

        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Clash of Titans: ADIEU vs. CRANE vs. SALET", 
            [
                "Humans love 'ADIEU' to find vowels quickly.", 
                "Vowels are common but don't prune words efficiently.", 
                "Algorithms prefer 'SALET' for its powerful consonant placement.", 
                "'SALET' leaves fewer than 20 words on average.", 
                "Consonants provide better structural information than vowels."
            ]
        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Practical Application: Your 5-Minute Strategy"
        lines = [
            "Prioritize high-frequency consonants in your opening moves.",
            "Avoid repeating letters across your first two guesses.",
            "Play for information, not just for the lucky win."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Pre-create common colors
        COLOR_CONSONANT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_NO_REPEAT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_CHEAT_SHEET = "#D4AF37"
        COLOR_SOLVED = "#6AAA64"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Consonants Icons
        consonants = ["S", "T", "R", "L", "N"]
        consonant_icons = VGroup()
        for char in consonants:
            circ = Circle(radius=0.4, color=COLOR_CONSONANT)
            txt = Text(char, font_size=32, color=COLOR_CONSONANT)
            consonant_icons.add(VGroup(circ, txt))
        
        consonant_icons.arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=3, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(consonant_icons, "A2", "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(consonant_icons))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # No-repeat sign
        no_repeat_circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=COLOR_NO_REPEAT, stroke_width=8)
        no_repeat_slash = Line(
            start=no_repeat_circle.point_at_angle(135 * DEGREES),
            end=no_repeat_circle.point_at_angle(-45 * DEGREES),
            color=COLOR_NO_REPEAT,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        
        # Representative "Repeated Letter" visual (e.g. 'E' and 'E')
        ee_text = Text("E ... E", color=COLOR_NO_REPEAT, font_size=36)
        no_repeat_group = VGroup(no_repeat_circle, no_repeat_slash, ee_text)
        self.place_in_area(no_repeat_group, "A5", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(no_repeat_circle), Create(no_repeat_slash), Write(ee_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Golden Cheat Sheet Box
        cheat_sheet_bg = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2.0, color=COLOR_CHEAT_SHEET, stroke_width=4)
        cheat_sheet_title = Text("CHEAT SHEET", font_size=20, color=COLOR_CHEAT_SHEET).next_to(cheat_sheet_bg.get_top(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        words = VGroup(
            Text("SLATE", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("CRANE", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("TRACE", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2).next_to(cheat_sheet_title, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        cheat_sheet = VGroup(cheat_sheet_bg, cheat_sheet_title, words)
        self.place_in_area(cheat_sheet, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Magnifying Glass zooming into a Solved Grid
        # Create a simplified 3x3 grid section for the zoom
        grid_rows = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            row = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_SOLVED if i == 2 else GRAY) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            grid_rows.add(row)
        grid_rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        # Final "Solved" state label
        solved_text = Text("SOLVED", font_size=20, color=COLOR_SOLVED).next_to(grid_rows, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        solved_ui = VGroup(grid_rows, solved_text)
        self.place_in_area(solved_ui, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Magnifying Glass
        mag_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        mag_handle = Line(mag_circle.point_at_angle(-45 * DEGREES), mag_circle.point_at_angle(-45 * DEGREES) + (0.4 * DOWN + 0.4 * RIGHT), color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        magnifying_glass = VGroup(mag_circle, mag_handle)
        
        # Start magnifying glass over the grid and scale up
        magnifying_glass.move_to(solved_ui.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cheat_sheet))
        self.play(FadeIn(solved_ui))
        self.play(magnifying_glass.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(magnifying_glass.animate.scale(1/1.5), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Mastering the Wordle Opening: An Algorithmic Deep Dive
outline.target_audience: University students and puzzle enthusiasts with a basic interest in logic and data science.

sections.title: The Objective: Shrinking the Search Space
sections.content: Introduce Wordle mechanics as a process of elimination. The goal of the first move isn't just to 'get letters right,' but to discard as many of the 2,315 possible secret words as possible. Visual: A large cloud of 2,315 dots representing words, which shrinks after a guess.
sections.example: If you guess 'FUZZY' and get all grey, you only eliminate a few words. If you guess 'TRACE' and get all grey, you eliminate hundreds of possibilities because T, R, A, C, and E are high-frequency letters.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Understanding Entropy and Information Theory
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Bits of Information.' Information is the measure of how much uncertainty is reduced. Use a binary tree graphic to show how each bit of information cuts the remaining possibilities in half.
sections.example: Think of a 'Guess Who?' game. Asking 'Is the character a person?' provides 0 bits (useless), but 'Is the character wearing glasses?' splits the group, providing higher entropy.

sections.title: The Math: The 243 Possible Feedback Patterns
sections.content: Explain that Wordle provides 3 possible colors (Grey, Yellow, Green) for 5 positions. This creates 3^5 (243) unique color patterns. A good starting word distributes the 2,315 possible answers as evenly as possible across these 243 'buckets.' Visual: A histogram showing the distribution of words into color buckets.
sections.example: A bad word like 'MAMMA' puts almost all secret words into one or two buckets. A good word like 'SALET' spreads the hidden words thin across many different color patterns.

sections.title: Calculating Expected Information Gain (EIG)
sections.content: Present the formula for Expected Information (Entropy = Σ p * log2(1/p)). Explain that we want the word that yields the highest average 'bits' across all possible secret words. Visual: A character 'Bit-Bot' calculating the probability of each color pattern for the word 'CRANE'.
sections.example: If 'CRANE' results in a 'Green C' 10% of the time and 'All Grey' 20% of the time, we calculate the average surprise (entropy) we expect to get from those results.

sections.title: The Clash of Titans: ADIEU vs. CRANE vs. SALET
sections.content: Compare popular human strategies vs. algorithmic optimal strategies. Many humans use 'ADIEU' to find vowels, but algorithms prefer 'SALET' or 'CRANE' because consonants like R, S, and T are more effective at narrowing down the specific word structure. Visual: A leaderboard comparing the average number of steps to solve.
sections.example: Using 'ADIEU' identifies vowels quickly but often leaves 50+ possible words. Using 'SALET' usually leaves fewer than 20 possibilities because it tests letter positions more efficiently.

sections.title: Practical Application: Your 5-Minute Strategy
sections.content: Summarize the takeaway: (1) Use high-frequency consonants, (2) Avoid repeating letters in the first two guesses, (3) Focus on information over 'getting it right' on turn one. Visual: A quick 'cheat sheet' graphic showing top-tier openers like 'TAROT', 'SLATE', and 'CRANE'.
sections.example: Imagine you are a detective. Don't try to guess the killer's name immediately; ask the questions that eliminate the most suspects at once.
